summary: A brick lighthouse of 1858 on a 3.5-acre rock at Death's Door; its keeper waded into the surf in 1892 to save a schooner's crew. Now a closed bird sanctuary.

access.note: Island is part of Green Bay National Wildlife Refuge, closed to the public; seen from the water.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in text: Nichols wreck date (LSS 28 Oct 1892 vs nomination 4 Nov), numbers saved (8 vs 6), Gilmore name/date, house size, first Plum light date, fog building date (1900 est. vs 1904). Lighthouse Friends and the FOPPI page are used for events with no primary source reachable; 1858-1875 Light-House Board reports are not in the local corpus. Fog-signal hours from LHB volumes whose page numbers are unreliable (scan pages only). The Rohn log quotation is in the 1937 Bulletin and the FOPPI page, both read. Boyce death described minimally. Pulse article date of closed-to-public status is 2022-2023; Friends report 2025/2026 roof repairs. Friends call Boyce suicide cause; not detailed in story. Checker 2026-10-27: first Plum Island light date differs across sources (nomination 1850, Lighthouse Friends 1848, Friends implied 1849) and is stated as a disagreement. Bulletin page numbers are PDF pages. The Medal list names Martin Knudsen in OCR-mixed columns; matched to Port des Mortes keeper and the Pilot Island Nichols entry. The 1983 NRHP listing event was removed (no fetched source gives the listing year).
